title: What Is a Tax Engine? How It Works and Why Your Business Needs One
summary: Vertex is the leading and most-trusted provider of comprehensive, integrated tax technology solutions, having helped 10,000+ businesses since 1978.
body_text: Resources Library What Is a Tax Engine? How It Works and Why Your Business Needs One As tax complexity grows, businesses need a better way to apply the right tax consistently across systems, jurisdictions, and transactions. Learn how tax engines work and why they play a critical role in modern tax automation. June 24, 2019 Share Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Linkedin Share via Email What Is a Tax Engine? How It Works and Why Your Business Needs One With more than 20,000 tax jurisdictions worldwide—each with its own rates, rules, and reporting requirements that can change frequently—it can be difficult to determine the correct tax for every transaction. Determining the correct tax becomes even more challenging as your business expands. New products, new markets, and new systems often mean more tax rules to manage. What once worked in a single system can become difficult to maintain across multiple ERP, e-commerce, procurement, and financial applications. Manual processes and disconnected systems can no longer keep pace. That's why many businesses turn to a tax engine. What Is a Tax Engine? A tax engine is software that automates tax determination by calculating and applying the correct indirect tax —such as sales tax, consumer use tax, VAT, or GST—on a transaction. To do this, it evaluates information such as the product being sold, customer location, applicable tax rules, and jurisdictional requirements. Tax determination is often more complex than it appears. Take a KitKat, for example. Because it contains a wafer, some jurisdictions classify it as a baked good and apply different tax rules. Or consider a face or body lotion that contains SPF. In some locations, it may qualify for tax treatment similar to sunscreen. These kinds of nuances exist across countless products and jurisdictions. The tax applied to a purchase can vary based on what you're selling, where you're selling it, who is buying it, and the local tax rules in effect. A tax engine automatically evaluates those variables and determines the appropriate tax. How Does a Tax Engine Work? When a transaction is created in an ERP, e-commerce, procurement, or financial system, the transaction details are sent to the tax engine in real time. The tax engine evaluates information such as: Product or service type Customer information Ship-to and bill-to locations Applicable tax rules and rates Jurisdiction-specific requirements Using that information, the tax engine determines the appropriate tax and sends the calculated tax amount back to the originating system so the transaction can be completed. Tax engines are commonly integrated with ERP, e-commerce, procurement, and financial systems. Instead of maintaining tax rules and calculations separately across multiple applications, you can manage them in one place. What Are the Benefits of Using a Tax Engine? A tax engine helps simplify tax determination by centralizing tax rules and calculations in one place. Instead of managing tax across multiple systems, you can apply tax more efficiently across your business. Key benefits include: Improved tax accuracy by automatically applying the appropriate tax rules Reduced risk and audit exposure through more consistent tax determination and better visibility into tax decisions Less manual effort by automating tax calculations and reducing rework Centralized control by managing tax rules and calculations in one place Support for business growth as you expand into new markets, products, channels, and systems Whether you're responsible for tax, finance, or IT, a tax engine can help reduce manual effort, improve visibility, and create a more scalable approach to managing tax across the business. Why Getting Tax Right Upfront Matters Getting tax right at the start of a transaction matters. When tax is calculated incorrectly, the impact doesn't stop there. Errors can create additional work later in the process, leading to reporting issues, compliance challenges , audit risk, and costly corrections. The benefits of accurate tax determination extend far beyond the transaction itself. It supports reporting, audits, compliance, and broader tax and finance operations. As tax complexity grows, organizations need a reliable way to apply tax consistently and accurately across the business. Without a centralized approach to tax determination, you may face: Financial risk from underpayments, overpayments, penalties, interest assessments, and costly remediation efforts Operational inefficiencies caused by manual reviews, reconciliations, exception handling, and rework Technology challenges associated with maintaining tax logic across multiple systems and keeping tax rules up to date Reduced confidence in tax accuracy when different systems rely on different tax logic or outdated rules What Should You Look for in a Tax Engine? Not all tax engines are the same. As you evaluate solutions , consider whether they can support your business today while adapting to future growth and regulatory change. As you compare solutions, here are a few capabilities to look for: Accurate and up-to-date tax content that keeps pace with changing regulations and jurisdictional requirements. Integration with your business systems , including ERP, e-commerce, procurement, and financial applications. Centralized control of tax rules and calculations so tax can be managed consistently across your organization. Scalability to support growth , including new jurisdictions, products, channels, systems, and business models. Visibility and audit readiness , with clear reporting and insight into how tax decisions are being made. AI-enabled productivity tools that help automate complex tax tasks and improve efficiency. Support for the broader tax lifecycle , including related tax, compliance, reporting, and exemption management processes. Deployment flexibility to align with your organization's performance, security, and operational requirements. A tax engine should do more than automate calculations. It should help you create a more scalable and sustainable approach to tax determination as complexity increases. Is It Time to Invest in a Tax Engine? You may reach a point where your current approach to managing tax can no longer keep up with your business. If any of the following situations sound familiar, it may be time to evaluate whether a tax engine can help: Expanding into new regions or jurisdictions Managing tax across multiple systems or ERPs Addressing recurring audit or compliance challenges Experiencing increasing transaction volumes Preparing for ERP modernization initiatives Launching new e-commerce or digital business models If several of these challenges sound familiar, it may be a sign that your current approach to tax determination is no longer keeping pace with your business. title: Boston Event Spreads Battery Safety Awareness
summary: On July 22, in partnership with the National Waste and Recycling Association, ReSource Waste Services, and the Boston Fire Department, Casella helped host a battery take-back event in the Boston neighborhood of West Roxbury, MA.
body_text: 2026-07-27 14:04 Press release Boston Event Spreads Battery Safety Awareness On July 22, in partnership with the National Waste and Recycling Association , ReSource Waste Services, and the Boston Fire Department, Casella helped host a battery take-back event in the Boston neighborhood of West Roxbury, MA, which brought together residents, industry partners, municipal officials, and safety advocates around a simple but important goal: keeping batteries out of the trash. During the event, approximately 1,000 pounds of batteries were collected for safe recycling and proper management. Just as importantly, volunteers and organizers had dozens of meaningful conversations with community members about the growing importance of battery safety and why batteries should never be placed in household trash or recycling bins. Every battery collected represents one less potential fire risk in collection trucks, recycling facilities, and waste processing operations, while helping recover valuable materials for reuse. The batteries collected will be shipped through the Battery Network, sorted, and processed to recover as much of the recyclable material as possible. The event is another reminder that small actions can have a significant impact on public safety, environmental stewardship, and protecting the workers who keep our communities clean. To find out where to turn in your batteries and learn more about how you can help spread awareness of this growing problem, please visit www.batterysafetynow.org . Topics: Recycling Community About Casella Waste Systems, Inc. Casella Waste Systems, Inc., headquartered in Rutland, Vermont, is one of the largest recyclers and most experienced fully integrated resource management companies in the Eastern United States. Founded in 1975 as a single truck collection service, Casella has grown its operations to provide solid waste collection and disposal, transfer, recycling, and organics services to more than one million residential, commercial, municipal, institutional, and industrial customers and provides professional resource management services to over 10,000 customer locations in more than 40 states. title: KindlyMD Approved for Options Trading on Nasdaq

body_text: Salt Lake City, UTAH – September 10, 2025 – KindlyMD, Inc. (NASDAQ: NAKA) (“KindlyMD” or “the Company”), a provider of integrated healthcare services and a Bitcoin treasury vehicle via its subsidiary Nakamoto Holdings (“Nakamoto”), today announced that options on its common stock have been approved for trading tomorrow on the Nasdaq Options Market (“Nasdaq”). Trading of KindlyMD options will commence under the ticker symbol “NAKA” and includes a range of standard expiration dates and strike prices. The introduction of listed options is expected to broaden investor visibility and provide shareholders with additional tools to manage risk, leverage positions, and engage with KindlyMD’s long-term growth strategy. “The commencement of options trading on the Nasdaq marks another important milestone for KindlyMD, further enhancing our capital markets presence and providing shareholders with greater flexibility in how they invest in the Nakamoto story,” said David Bailey, Chairman and CEO of KindlyMD. Formed in 2019, KindlyMD leverages data analysis to deliver evidence-based, personalized solutions in order to reduce opioid use, improve health outcomes faster, and provide value based, algorithmic guidance on the use of alternative medicine in healthcare. In August 2025, KindlyMD completed its merger with Nakamoto Holdings Inc., a Bitcoin-native holding company. This strategic partnership formed a public Bitcoin treasury strategy that unites KindlyMD's healthcare expertise with Nakamoto's vision of integrating Bitcoin into global capital markets, creating a diversified entity focused on both healthcare innovation and Bitcoin treasury management. title: What is Vendor Management? Processes, Challenges & Tools
summary: All-in-one Spend Management platform for Procure-to-Pay, Corporate Cards, Accounts Payable Automation, Vendor Payouts, Reimbursements and more!
body_text: Vendor management is about how you select, onboard, track, and work with your suppliers. Without a defined process, you risk delays, missed deadlines, compliance issues, and extra costs. A structured approach helps you stay organised, manage contracts, and measure performance more effectively. According to Gartner’s 2024 report , by 2027, 50% of companies will use AI tools to support vendor negotiations. This shows how much value businesses are placing on smarter vendor management. In this blog, you’ll learn what vendor management means, how the process works, and how the right approach can help you work more efficiently with your vendors. Key Takeaways Vendor management involves selecting, onboarding, and monitoring vendors to ensure quality and cost control. Clear communication and performance tracking help build strong vendor relationships. Technology like vendor management systems automates workflows and improves data accuracy. Common challenges include compliance risks, managing multiple vendors, and payment delays. Common challenges include handling multiple vendors, delayed payments, and regulatory risks. What Is Vendor Management? Vendor management is how you handle every part of working with your suppliers. It helps you stay in control of costs, timelines, performance, and compliance. Instead of reacting to issues, you set clear expectations from the start and track how vendors deliver over time. Here’s what vendor management typically includes: Vendor selection : Choosing the right suppliers based on price, quality, and reliability Contract management : Defining terms, timelines, and responsibilities Performance tracking : Monitoring delivery, service levels, and results Risk management : Identifying and addressing compliance or operational risks Ongoing communication : Keeping vendors aligned with your goals When done right, vendor management helps you build long-term, efficient, and accountable supplier relationships. Why Is Vendor Management Important? Without effective vendor management, your company could face delays, increased costs, and compliance issues that disrupt both daily operations and long-term growth. Here’s why managing your vendors well matters: Maintain Cost Efficiency : By negotiating competitive prices and favourable contract terms, you keep your production and operational costs under control. This directly improves your bottom line. Ensure Quality Control : Regularly monitoring vendors helps guarantee that the materials and services you receive meet your quality standards, reducing the risk of product defects or service failures. Mitigate Sourcing Risks : Identifying potential problems early—such as a vendor’s financial instability or inability to meet delivery schedules—allows you to take preventive actions, like finding alternative suppliers before disruptions occur. Stay Compliant : Vendor management ensures that your suppliers follow legal regulations and your company’s policies. This protects your business from legal risks and helps maintain industry certifications. Enable Seamless Scalability : A strong vendor management process allows your business to quickly adapt to changes in demand, whether seasonal or market-driven, ensuring uninterrupted supply and service. Improve Supply Chain Reliability : Consistent vendor oversight minimises the chances of delays or disruptions, supporting the timely delivery of goods and services. Build Strong Vendor Relationships : Effective communication and collaboration with your vendors lead to long-term partnerships, better service, and potential cost savings. Prevent Financial Errors : Keeping track of invoices and contracts helps avoid payment mistakes and contract discrepancies that could harm your financial health. Maintain Transparency and Accountability : Using regular reports and KPIs to assess vendor performance promotes transparency, helping you make informed decisions and improve supplier management. By investing in vendor management, you protect your business from risks, reduce costs, and build a dependable supply chain that supports your growth ambitions. Also Read: Vendor Relations: The Hidden Benefit of Faster Payments Vendor Management Process: Step-by-Step A structured vendor management process is essential for maintaining smooth supplier relationships and ensuring your business operates without interruptions. By following clear steps, you can select the right vendors, maintain quality and compliance, and reduce risks that could impact your operations. 1. Vendor Selection Shortlist suppliers based on more than just cost. Look for proven delivery timelines, quality standards, communication responsiveness, and financial stability. Ask for references or case studies when the stakes are high. A poor vendor at this stage becomes a bigger problem later. 2. Contract Negotiation Draft contracts that remove ambiguity. Define payment terms, delivery expectations, penalties for delays, renewal clauses, and service levels in detail. Avoid soft language. Clear terms protect both parties and reduce friction when issues arise. 3. Vendor Onboarding Collect all required documentation, such as licenses, tax information, payment instructions, and NDAs, before adding the vendor to your systems. Delays in onboarding often stem from missing paperwork. A checklist-driven process ensures compliance from the start. 4. Performance Monitoring Track vendor KPIs like delivery accuracy, defect rates, responsiveness, and cost adherence. Use regular reviews to flag patterns early. Consistently underperforming vendors should be escalated or replaced. 5. Risk Monitoring and Management Avoid relying on a single vendor or region for critical supplies. Monitor geopolitical, financial, and legal risks that could impact performance. Build backup options or dual-source when needed, especially for high-dependency categories. 6. Payment Management Late payments damage relationships and delay future deliveries. Ensure invoices are matched to contracts and approved promptly. Automating this process reduces errors, speeds up approvals, and strengthens vendor trust. Next, it's important to know that even with a good process, some challenges can arise. Understanding these helps you stay prepared. Challenges of Vendor Management While vendor management is critical for business success, it comes with several challenges that can complicate the process: Non-compliance Risk: Not all vendors consistently meet your company’s standards. If you rely on a limited number of suppliers, a non-compliant vendor can delay projects or force costly changes like onboarding new vendors or cancelling contracts. Vendor Reputation Concerns: Conduct thorough background checks before partnering with vendors. Gathering feedback, testimonials, and conducting due diligence reports helps ensure the vendor is financially stable and has a trustworthy track record, reducing surprises later. Managing Price Increases: Even if you have a good relationship with a vendor, contract terms and pricing can change. Staying alert to cost increases or unfavourable changes is necessary to maintain alignment with your business goals. Too Many Vendors: Handling too many vendors or duplicates can overwhelm your team and systems. Choosing the right vendors early on helps simplify management and improve efficiency. Limited Data Storage and Tracking: With hundreds of vendors onboarded, tracking their details accurately is challenging. Missing or incorrect vendor information can lead to confusion over invoices and delayed payments, making it difficult to maintain smooth operations. Late Payment Risks: Different vendors have varied payment terms and modes, which can cause payment delays. These delays often strain vendor relationships, risking service disruptions. Overcoming these challenges is easier with the right tools. Kodo’s spend management platform helps you centralise vendor information, automate workflows, and maintain real-time visibility into your vendor relationships. Simplify vendor tracking, ensure timely payments, and reduce risks all in one place. Best Practices for Vendor Management Implementing effective vendor management requires more than just following a process. Adopting best practises can help you build strong, lasting partnerships and keep your supply chain efficient and resilient. Define Clear Expectations : Set transparent goals and performance metrics from the start. Communicate your quality standards, delivery timelines, and compliance requirements clearly to avoid misunderstandings. Maintain Open Communication: Regular and honest communication with vendors helps address issues early and fosters collaboration. Schedule periodic reviews and encourage feedback to strengthen relationships. Use Data to Make Decisions: Use performance data and analytics to monitor vendor reliability, costs, and compliance. Data-driven insights enable you to make informed choices and identify areas for improvement. Build Strong Relationships: Treat your vendors as partners rather than just suppliers. Building trust and mutual respect can lead to better service, favourable terms, and quicker problem resolution. Diversify Your Vendor Base: Avoid dependency on a single vendor or region to reduce supply chain risks. Maintaining multiple reliable vendors helps ensure continuity even if one vendor faces challenges. Regularly Review and Update Contracts: Keep your contracts up to date to reflect changing business needs and market conditions. Periodic reviews allow renegotiation of terms and inclusion of new compliance requirements. Following these best practices will help you manage vendors more efficiently, control costs, and minimise risks, ultimately supporting your business growth and operational stability. Moving on, learn how technology plays an important role in simplifying and improving how you manage vendors. Also Read: Understanding Invoice Processing: Key Steps and Benefits Role of Technology in Vendor Management Technology has transformed vendor management by making processes more efficient, transparent, and less prone to error. Vendor Management Systems (VMS) are digital platforms that centralise all vendor-related activities from onboarding and contract tracking to compliance and performance monitoring, providing better visibility and control across the entire vendor lifecycle. Key features of a VMS include: A centralised vendor database stores all vendor data, documents, and contracts in one easily accessible location, ensuring nothing gets lost or overlooked. Automated workflows streamline tasks such as vendor onboarding, approvals, and updates, reducing manual effort and minimising delays. Contract and renewal alerts provide timely reminders of upcoming deadlines and key milestones, helping you avoid missed obligations and costly oversights. Real-time reporting delivers live dashboards and customizable reports so you can continuously monitor vendor performance and spending. Built-in compliance checks automatically flag missing documents or expired certifications, keeping your vendor relationships audit-ready at all times. Integration with ERP and finance systems syncs vendor data seamlessly with your accounting and procurement tools, ensuring smoother transactions and fewer errors. With these technology features in mind, it’s important to choose tools that not only manage vendor data but also streamline payment processes and spending controls. Invoice Management : Organise and store invoices and receipts digitally, making record-keeping and audits easier. Real-Time Spend Tracking: Access up-to-date spending insights to help you stay on budget and make informed decisions. Vendor Relationship Support: Ensure payments are made on time and keep communication clear to build trust and strengthen partnerships. Wrapping Up Effective vendor management is key to controlling costs, reducing risks, and building strong supplier relationships. By adopting a structured process and using the right technology, you can simplify your operations and improve overall efficiency. Kodo offers a comprehensive platform that automates vendor workflows, ensures compliance, and provides real-time spend visibility. This helps you manage vendors with greater ease and confidence. Vendor management is the process of overseeing and coordinating your relationships with suppliers. It involves selecting vendors, managing contracts, monitoring performance, ensuring compliance, and maintaining communication to meet your business needs effectively. 2. What are the four stages of vendor management? The four main stages are: Vendor Selection – Choosing the right suppliers based on criteria like quality and price Contract Negotiation – Setting terms and agreements Performance Management – Tracking and evaluating vendor delivery and quality Relationship Management – Maintaining ongoing communication and resolving issues 3. title: Court-Appointed Monitor Finds ICE Failed to Provide Adequate Medical Care, in Violation of Court Order
summary: New report provides damning indictment of ICE’s abuses at California’s largest ICE detention center in first-ever court appointed investigation of...
body_text: Court-Appointed Monitor Finds ICE Failed to Provide Adequate Medical Care, in Violation of Court Order New report provides damning indictment of ICE’s abuses at California’s largest ICE detention center in first-ever court appointed investigation of full scope of medical care at immigration detention facility July 28, 2026 8:00 am Media Contact media@aclu.org (212) 549-2666 125 Broad Street 18th Floor New York, NY 10004 United States SAN FRANCISCO – Attorneys at the Prison Law Office, Keker, Van Nest & Peters LLP, and the American Civil Liberties Union filed a public report from a court-appointed monitor late last night that finds ICE is failing to comply with a preliminary injunction requiring it to provide a constitutionally adequate healthcare system at the California City Detention Facility. This marks the first time a court-appointed neutral party has investigated the full scope of the delivery of medical care at an ICE detention center. The report is based on a three-day site inspection, interviews with more than a dozen staff and 40 patients, and reviews of 141 patient medical records and thousands of pages of documents produced by ICE and CoreCivic, the private prison company operating the facility. The report’s findings include: Missing or incomplete medical intake screenings for existing conditions, communicable diseases, and chronic illnesses that require immediate or constant treatment Delayed and denied clinical care, including gaps in emergency care, mental health care, and specialty referrals Failure to provide timely access to prescribed medications and to identify and support patients with disabilities Inadequate staffing, incomplete training, a lack of on-site management, and insufficient clinical oversight. The external monitor concludes that access to healthcare is inadequate, making California City “an unsafe environment.” “The facility lacks a reliable system to consistently provide adequate healthcare, placing individuals at serious risk of both immediate and long-term harm,” the report states. “This pattern indicates broader problems in the facility’s health care delivery system rather than occasional lapses in care.” The report’s conclusions make clear that ICE is violating a February federal court order requiring the agency to provide adequate medical care to individuals detained at California City. Gustavo Guevara Alarcon spent nine months at the facility and experienced the conditions there firsthand. “California City failed to provide even the most basic medical care,” he said “I watched people pass out in their cells. I watched someone wait months to see an oncologist and begin lifesaving treatment. I was frequently denied basic over-the-counter medication like ibuprofen and had requests for reasonable medical accommodations repeatedly denied. No one should be subject to this kind of treatment, and certainly not at the hands of the government.” The California City Detention Facility is California’s largest ICE detention center and holds nearly 1,500 people. It is a remote facility, located in the Mojave Desert. Soon after its opening in Fall 2025, people detained at the facility sued the Trump administration and petitioned a federal court to require ICE to provide adequate medical care and improve overall conditions. In February of this year, a federal judge certified the case as a class action and granted a preliminary injunction to improve conditions for those detained at the facility. Among other things, the order required ICE to provide a functional healthcare system and appointed an external monitor for a four-month period to assess compliance and make a report and recommendations to the Court. Fernando Viera Reyes is currently being held at the California City Detention Facility. He has now been diagnosed with metastatic prostate cancer, but it took five months for California City to get him a biopsy to diagnose his cancer, and another month before he was told the result. “For months, I couldn’t move, sleep, or even use the bathroom without being in extreme pain. It wasn’t until we filed this class action lawsuit and had a court order that staff at California City finally got me to a specialist. By the time I received my official diagnosis, the cancer had spread all over my body. If my ability to get cancer treatment is in the hands of this same staff, I’m scared I’ll be left without the healthcare I need. It feels like we’re being treated like we don’t have any value, but we’re all human beings, and we deserve life-saving treatment just like anyone else.” Additional quotes from Plaintiffs and co-counsel are as follows: Sokhean Keo is currently in the California City Detention Facility. “If there is no change to this system, sick people are going to die. I haven’t been able to get care for my chronic conditions because ICE refuses to work with the doctors I need to see. When I finally saw a doctor for an infection, I didn’t receive the medication they prescribed. We should be able to leave this place in one piece, not sicker than we came in.” Alejandro Mendiola Escutia has been in the California City Detention Facility for nine months. “When I arrived at California City, they confiscated my prescribed medication and the back and knee braces that were given to me by a doctor. I had to make a makeshift knee brace using my socks just to tolerate the pain. These examples just go on and on. The cruelty we’re facing is a living nightmare. We’re not asking for anything special, just asking for basic medical care." “ICE has shown time and time again that it is not putting any care into the health and safety of the people detained at the California City Detention Facility, even when explicitly required by the court,” said Carmen Iguina González, Deputy Director for Immigration Detention of the ACLU National Prison Project . “This report has made it abundantly clear that the facility is unfit to hold anyone in detention if it can’t meet their basic needs. We will continue our work to ensure that every single person detained at this facility receives the medical care they need.” “This report confirms what thousands of people have experienced firsthand: in every area of health care, California City is failing,” said Tess Borden, Managing Attorney at the Prison Law Office. “The external monitor’s findings tell a nightmarish story – psychiatric patients left without follow-up, medication and culture specimens improperly stored, specialist appointments that were missed or never scheduled. But his recommendations offer a path forward, and we’ll keep fighting for the care the Constitution demands.” “The monitor’s findings confirm that the failures at California City are hardly isolated incidents; they are systemic, ongoing, and dangerous,” Cody Harris, partner with Keker, Van Nest & Peters, said. “People detained at California City have been denied timely medical care and placed at serious risk because the facility lacks the staffing and infrastructure required to provide adequate healthcare. This conduct is especially egregious because the individuals are being held in civil detention, and the government is under court order to remedy these unconstitutional conditions.” This report can be found online here: https://www.aclu.org/documents/report-of-the-external-monitor-on-medical-care-at-california-city-detention-facility

title: The 11 Best Low-Effort Ways to Stay Social and Cool This Summer
summary: Discover low-effort indoor social activities for seniors that help reduce loneliness, support emotional well-being, and make it easier to stay connected during hot weather.
body_text: Record-breaking high temperatures have made this a challenging summer across much of the country. When the heat index stays high day after day, health experts often recommend older adults limit time outdoors to prevent dehydration, heat stroke, and falls. But that can also mean spending more time at home, feeling bored and alone. Fortunately, staying connected doesn't have to involve strenuous activities or long days in the sun. There are plenty of indoor activities for seniors that are enjoyable, low-energy, and inside where it's cool and comfortable. Keep reading for ideas on how to stay connected with friends while beating the heat this summer. Why Social Activities for Seniors Matter Research shows that maintaining friendships and participating in regular social activities supports emotional well-being, reduces feelings of loneliness , and even contributes to better physical health as we age. Having reasons to leave the house – even just once or twice a week – helps build routine, improve mood, and provide meaningful opportunities to connect with others. But if that sounds like a lot of effort, especially in the summer, we have good news. Staying social doesn't have to require lots of time or energy to reap the same sorts of benefits. 1. Meet a Friend Somewhere with AC You don't need an all-day outdoor adventure to enjoy someone's company. Meeting a friend for lunch, coffee, or even dessert can be one of the simplest summer activities for seniors. Restaurants, cafés, and diners are comfortable, air-conditioned places to sit, catch up, and enjoy a change of scenery without worrying about the heat. If afternoons are hottest where you live, consider an early lunch or mid-morning coffee date to minimize your exposure to the heat. Bonus: many local restaurants also offer early bird specials that make lunch dates more affordable. 2. Visit Your Local Senior Center If it's been a while since you've checked out your local senior center, you may be surprised by everything they have on the calendar! Many senior center activities are designed specifically for older adults looking to stay active socially without overexerting themselves in the heat, such as: Card games Bingo Craft classes Exercise classes designed for older adults Educational talks Ice cream socials Movie afternoons These programs are among the best social activities for senior citizens because everyone is open-minded to meet people, connect, and have fun. They’re designed to be welcoming, even if you're attending alone. 3. Attend Indoor Community Events Around Town Libraries, museums, churches, recreation centers, and community organizations often host free or inexpensive programs throughout the summer. And most events last only an hour or two, making them perfect for low-energy outings. Popular community indoor activities for seniors include: Book clubs Guest speakers Movie afternoons Local history presentations Craft workshops Indoor concerts Art exhibits Community game nights If you're not sure where to start, check your local library's event calendar, your city's parks and recreation department, nearby museums, community centers, places of worship, or your local newspaper's community events calendar. Many communities also have Facebook groups or neighborhood websites where upcoming events are shared. 4. Start a Weekly Coffee Tradition You don't need a special occasion to see someone! Choose one morning each week to meet the same friend, neighbor, sibling, or grandchild for coffee. Don’t like coffee? Any recurring activity works! Maybe every Tuesday evening is cookies and tea with a neighbor. Perhaps Friday becomes lunch with a sibling. Or Sunday afternoons are reserved for playing cards with friends. Small traditions remove the pressure of constantly making plans and gives you and your loved ones something to look forward to. 5. Join an Indoor Hobby Group Making friends is easier when you have something in common already, like a shared hobby. Doing a hobby in a group makes conversations flow naturally. So look for local groups for your favorite hobbies… or try something new! Some indoor hobby ideas include painting, knitting, photography, genealogy, puzzles, or board games. Chances are there's a local group that shares your interests. Even attending once a month can help you build meaningful connections over time. 6. Try Online Social Activities for Seniors Some days, it's just too hot, or you don't have the energy to leave the house. And that's perfectly okay. There are plenty of online social activities for seniors that make it easy to stay connected from home. You could: Schedule weekly video chats with family members. Join a virtual book club. Attend an online church discussion. Take an online art or history class. Play virtual trivia with friends. Even one scheduled video call each week with familiar faces can make a big difference. Check out: 9 Best Tech for Seniors Living Alone 7. Never Underestimate a Phone Call Not every social activity needs a big event or destination. Sometimes a fifteen-minute conversation is the perfect way to boost your social battery while staying cool and relaxed indoors. Calling a friend, sibling, grandchild, or former coworker can brighten your day – and theirs. Some seniors enjoy creating a rotating "phone date" schedule with friends or siblings so everyone stays in touch regularly. It's one of the lowest-effort ways to stay socially active all year long. 8. Explore Indoor Activities for Seniors with Limited Mobility Being social doesn't have to mean pushing yourself physically. There are lots of indoor activities for seniors with limited mobility, specifically designed to be comfortable and accessible. Some great options include: Chair yoga Card clubs Painting classes Puzzle groups Cooking demonstrations Music appreciation programs Movie clubs Many senior centers, libraries, and community organizations intentionally design these activities to be accessible and welcoming for people with varying mobility levels. 9. Volunteer Somewhere Air Conditioned If you're looking for a greater sense of purpose, volunteering is a wonderful option. Helping others is one of the best ways to meet people and bring more meaning to your days. You could consider: Greeting visitors at museums Assisting at food pantries Helping libraries with events Answering phones for nonprofits Hospital gift shops Community information desks Planning community events Even volunteering just a few hours each month can expand your social circle while giving back to your community. 10. Beyond the physical benefits of staying active , these classes also provide a sense of community. Seeing familiar faces each week, chatting with instructors and fellow participants, and sharing a regular routine can help make exercise feel more social and enjoyable. You’ll find classes for chair yoga, functional fitness, strength training, and more – and there’s a social period at the end of each class where everyone chats and has fun! 11. Plan One Small Outing Each Week It's easy to think you need a packed social calendar. You don't. One fun outing each week is enough to make a meaningful difference. Whether that's meeting someone for lunch, browsing a museum, or just grabbing coffee with a friend, those little moments of connection add up over time. Instead of trying to fill every day, aim for one enjoyable outing each week. That could be: Lunch with a friend A library program A museum visit A senior center class Coffee after church An indoor farmers market Visiting a shopping mall for a leisurely walk Keeping expectations small makes it much easier to stay consistent throughout the summer. Consistency with manageable activities matters more than pushing yourself at huge events. How to Stay Socially Active in Retirement Many people wonder how to stay socially active in retirement, especially if driving has become more difficult or friends have moved away. The key isn't filling your calendar with activities every day. Instead, focus on creating easy routines that fit your energy level, interests, and the season you’re in. During the hottest months of the year, that often means prioritizing indoor spaces, shorter outings, and lots of phone conversations. Try to: Schedule one social activity each week. Reach out to one friend or family member every few days. Choose indoor activities during periods of extreme heat. Join groups built around interests you already enjoy. Accept invitations, even if it's only for a short time. Small, consistent moments of connection often have a bigger impact than occasional large events.
